source: APPP / MAFF-JICA — Rice Seed Production Manual (សៀវភៅមគ្គទេសក៍ផលិតកម្មពូជស្រូវ), 2014, Agricultural Productivity Promotion Project in West Tonle Sap, p.24
text: Weed control is emphasized from the earliest growth stage (nursery/establishment) through to harvest, because weeds — including broadleaf weeds, grass weeds and aquatic weeds — compete with the rice crop for nutrients and can also harbor insect pests and disease. Recommended practices: maintain a shallow water level (around 5 cm) as part of weed suppression; where weeds have already flowered/set seed they must be removed by hand before they can shed seed into the field or paddy; producers are told to score/rate the field's weed infestation; and the field should be checked and confirmed weed-free before harvest, since weed seed contaminating the harvested lot is a seed-quality defect (see seed quality standards).
